checks.finding: The degree bound, excess partitions, no-loop argument, cubic multigraph enumeration, positive path lengths, parity condition, original simplicity constraint and subdivision converse yield exactly B4, T221, alternating-double C4 and K4. B4 is a suppressed multigraph, not a simple core. Known generalized-theta inequalities are attributed; the universal residual density cases remain unproved here.

Positive weights, nonnegativity and full coordinate symmetry make vanishing binary diagonal marginals force U=0 for r>=3. The same-carrier qualification and essential hypotheses are retained, and no converse equivalence with arbitrary graph kernels is inferred.

Both iff directions are valid with w_S=(r-2)!u_S product(mu on S), E U=r(r-1)sum_S w_S and capacity w_S<=(r-2)!product(mu on S) precisely for U<=1. The r=2, insufficient support and zero-mass cases and the K4-minus-cd obstruction are correct. The final synthesis explicitly separates unrestricted nonnegative realization from the additional unit-capacity condition.

For at least two core edges the positive-support reduction, exact private-vertex count, increasing transform and maximizing-subgraph correspondence establish balancedness and strictness equivalence. Degenerate signed/undefined domains and one-edge cases are separated. The general transformation is credited to Nie-Spiro rather than presented as new mathematics.

Exact N+2 saturation forces every class to span and every later face to add exactly one point. Deleting points or face labels preserves connectivity. The inequalities cover arbitrary selected vertex-and-edge subgraphs, including isolates and small selected point counts. The t=3,x=1 plateau yields no proper equality case. Counts, cycle rank, examples and the failure when saturation is removed are correct.

The expected-copy/edge ratio, Markov deletion, edge concentration and thinning give the stated fixed-pattern asymptotics under the displayed probability hypotheses. The exponent gamma is independent of r. Deletion scale is correctly distinguished from first appearance and from an additional positive-excess gain or a matching upper bound.

The maximum-matching lift has pair coefficient 1/(r-1) for even r and 1/r for odd r, exact mean-one regularity and the displayed supremum bound. Positive edge-subset coefficients give the r^-66 relative gap and r^-Cr mean conditionally on the complete family. The pair average gives r^-132 gap with polynomial mean. The logarithmic excess factors are correct. Odd primes suffice for polynomial q selection; no all-prime-power or explicit D=1642 claim is introduced.

The frozen source-check record supports extractable fixed-D O_D(q^-1/6) rates, proper-edge flatness and regularity checks and polynomial size bounds. The final sources no longer claim rates are absent; complete synthesis, rational-prior uniformization and external-input validation remain separate. The stronger question correctly asks for polynomial alphabet and mean together with r^-66 gap, states that neither conditional route proves it, and gives a sufficient universal trade-off falsification criterion without claiming global novelty, openness or sharpness.

Actual support/edge partition and incidence-forest hypotheses justify leaf integration while counting each joint weight once. Core-root even-cycle profiles are squared path kernels with row mass p^k, yielding the pointwise bound by weighted Cauchy-Schwarz. Parent-side ports may be private. One-joint bouquets of copies of one fixed cycle follow by the core bound and Jensen. These are regular-kernel sufficient conditions and do not imply unrestricted Sidorenko assembly closure.

The cubic kernel values and centered moments, epsilon=1/2560000, negative covariance -epsilon^2 and Hcp=1/256+1/20480000 check exactly. The all-r lift is bounded and regular with the stated pair and triple marginals. The ternary opposite ordering has factor128 eta^8/6561. Together these prove both strict orderings at every r>=3. All two-copy counts are8edges,8r-9vertices and connected Levi rank2. Negative covariance remains distinct from a full density deficit.

The final story reflects the proven source endpoints, gives the three working directions explicit quantified scope, retains the stronger-graph/weaker-marginal distinction and exact counterexample standard, and separates the source-backed extraction task from the stronger normalization question. It does not raise the proved low-rank cutoff, assume assembly closure or advertise a new global open problem.

The comparison names three pinned primary-source benchmarks and exact documented formalization boundaries, attributes Li's earlier classification and Nie-Spiro's transform, and treats catalogue claims as source-described rather than independently accepted. No scalar weakest-paper ranking, model-capability comparison, whole-paper correctness verdict or journal promise is made. The seven companion citation keys support the cited fragments.
